prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Houston for AC repair?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” HVAC company for every Houston homeowner — the right choice depends on your neighborhood, your unit’s brand/age, how quickly you need service, and your budget. I can, however, help you pick a very good one and avoid bad hires. Quick summary + next steps:

What to do right now
- If you want immediate local recommendations, tell me your ZIP code (or neighborhood) and whether you need emergency service today — I can then suggest top-rated companies in your area to contact.
- If you want to choose on your own, use the checklist and questions below.

Checklist: how to choose a good Houston HVAC company
- Licensing & insurance: verify the contractor’s Texas HVAC registration/License and proof of general liability insurance and workers’ comp.
- Certifications: look for NATE-certified technicians and manufacturer-authorized dealer status for your AC brand (if applicable).
- Local reputation: check recent Google and Yelp reviews, Angi or HomeAdvisor scores, and BBB rating. Prefer companies with many recent positive reviews.
- Transparent pricing: get a written estimate with parts, labor, diagnostic fee, and any warranty terms clearly stated.
- Warranties: ask about parts warranty and labor warranty (30–365 days+ depending on company).
- Emergency availability: confirm after-hours/24-hour repairs and any extra fees.
- Communication & professionalism: tech arrives on time, in uniform, with a truck stocked with parts and clear explanations of the problem and options.
- Ask for references for similar jobs or a list of recent customers if you want extra assurance.

Questions to ask before hiring
- Are you licensed/registered in Texas? Can you provide the registration number?
- Are your technicians NATE-certified?
- What is your diagnostic fee and is it deducted from repair cost if I proceed?
- Do you provide a written estimate and a written warranty for labor and parts?
- Do you handle permits if the job requires one?
- How soon can you come? Do you offer emergency service?

Typical cost ranges in Houston (ballpark)
- Diagnostic fee: $75–$200
- Minor repairs (capacitor, contactor, thermostat): $100–$450
- Refrigerant recharge (if legal/appropriate): $150–$500
- Fan motor or blower repairs: $300–$900
- Compressor or major outdoor unit replacement: $1,000–$3,000+ (depending on system size and brand)
Prices vary widely by problem, unit size, and brand — get 2–3 written estimates for major work.

Red flags
- Demands full cash up front for routine repair
- No proper ID, license, or written estimate
- “Fill it with refrigerant” without diagnosing a leak (that’s a temporary fix and may be illegal if it hides a leak)
- Extremely low bid compared to others (may be poor parts or workmanship)

If you want, I can:
- Look up top-rated HVAC companies in your Houston ZIP and list 3–5 to call (I’ll need your ZIP).
- Draft a short script with questions to ask when you call.
- Help interpret estimates you receive.

Which would you like to do next?
